text:
alina: FYI CI linkchecker blew up after switching several pages to Docusaurus. Lots of broken fragment links coming from the migration guide and SDK examples.
noah: Can you paste one failing example? I want to see if it's the punctuation->slug change or something else.
docs-ci-bot: linkcheck: FAILED 1772100042: /docs/sdk/python#examples/getting-started -> 404
alina: That one used to be `#examples-(getting-started)` in MkDocs. Docusaurus slugifies it differently so the fragments don't match.
tess: We should avoid changing every heading in existing pages. Options: add per-page redirects in frontmatter, add rewrite step in CI to patch links before check, or update PRs that reference old anchors.
omar: Short-term: redirects for the high-traffic pages (sdk, migration) so external links don't break. Mid-term: a repo-wide migration script that rewrites internal markdown links to the Docusaurus slug style.
lee: I can add a pre-linkcheck job that runs a fast Python script to convert `(#... )` style anchors into docusaurus slugs and annotate the PR. That will keep the linkcheck green while authors update their PRs.
alina: Nice. Two more weird ones discovered: 1) headings with em-dashes generate two dashes in the slug, breaking older single-dash links; 2) code block titles (eg. ```py title="example.py"```) create internal anchors that used to be predictable but are now different.
tess: For code fence titles, we previously relied on a Babel plugin in MkDocs. Docusaurus treats titles as just part of the code block component and generates a different anchor. We should publish a short docs note for authors about how code-fence anchors changed.
omar: I'll open a small redirect PR for the migration pages and the top SDK page. alina, can you list the top 8 failing fragments so I don't miss any?
alina: Pasting quick list from failing job: `/docs/migration/v1-to-v2#why-upgrade`, `/docs/sdk/python#examples/getting-started`, `/docs/console/troubleshooting#rate-limits`, `/docs/examples/embeddings#usage-notes`, `/docs/advanced/kv-cache#implementation-details`, `/docs/guides/priv-deploy#networking-considerations`, `/docs/faq#billing-faq`, `/docs/samples/js#code-fence-example`
noah: For the rewrite, use the same slug algorithm as Docusaurus. Here's a tiny node snippet that matches what we want:
```js
const {slugify} = require('@docusaurus/utils');
console.log(slugify('Why upgrade? — migration notes'));
// -> why-upgrade-migration-notes
```
lee: Good. I'll port that logic to Python for the CI helper so it can run inline without node. Will also add `--report-only` mode for the first run.
tess: Also add a linter rule in the docs pre-commit to flag old-style anchor links and suggest the new slug. That should reduce future regressions.
omar: Sounds like an actionable plan. I'll land redirects PR (small) and include a changelog entry so external customers get a heads-up.
alina: I'll open the tracking PR with checklist: redirects PR, CI rewrite job, pre-commit linter, docs note about code-fence anchors, and a follow-up to update existing PRs.
noah: I'll help test the rewrite script against the whole docs tree and post results as a file in the PR.
lee: After the redirect PR merges, re-run the linkcheck; it should clear the big migration failures. Then we can iterate on the rewrite and linter.
alina: Thanks all. Goal: restore green docs CI before tomorrow's deploy so the release pipeline isn't blocked. :thumbsup:
